{{Short description|American spectroscopist (1936–2019)}}
'''Jon Torger Hougen''' (23 October 1936 in [[Sheboygan, Wisconsin|Sheboygan]] – 28 January 2019 in [[Taipei]]) was an American spectroscopist.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.wenigfh.com/obituaries/obituary-listings?obId=4150768|title=Jon Torger Hougen Obituary - Visitation & Funeral Information|website=www.wenigfh.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Hougen finished his undergraduate degree at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin]] in 1956.<ref name=":0" /> He obtained his master's and doctoral degrees at [[Harvard University]].<ref name=":0" /> He worked at Harvard under the research direction of [[William Moffitt]] and [[William Klemperer]].<ref name=":0" /> He started his career in 1960 as a postdoctorate fellow at the [[National Research Council of Canada]]<ref name=":0" /> in the [[Spectroscopy|molecular spectroscopy]] group of [[Gerhard Herzberg]]. He joined the staff at NRC in 1962 and supervised postdoctorate 
fellows [[James Kay Graham Watson|J.K.G.Watson]] and [[Philip Bunker]]. In 1967 he joined the [[National Bureau of Standards]] (now the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]], or NIST).<ref name=":0" /> He started there as a member of D.R. Lide's [[Microwave spectroscopy|microwave]] and [[Infrared spectroscopy|infrared]] group.<ref name=":0" /> Later, he was the chief of the molecular spectroscopy section.<ref name=":0" /> In 1984, he was named a Senior Research Fellow of NIST.<ref name=":0" /> For a year, he served as acting chief of the molecular physics division.<ref name=":0" /> After retiring in 2001, he continued his research as a NIST Scientist Emeritus.<ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
His research focused on quantum mechanical and group theoretical calculations of quantities related to molecular spectroscopy.<ref name=":0" />

Three of his most-cited publications are:

*{{cite journal |last1=Hougen |first1=Jon T. |title=Rotational Energy Levels of a Linear Triatomic Molecule in a Π Electronic State |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=15 January 1962 |volume=36 |issue=2 |pages=519–534 |doi=10.1063/1.1732544 |bibcode=1962JChPh..36..519H }}
*{{cite journal |last1=Hougen |first1=J.T. |last2=Bunker |first2=P.R. |last3=Johns |first3=J.W.C. |title=The vibration-rotation problem in triatomic molecules allowing for a large-amplitude bending vibration |journal=Journal of Molecular Spectroscopy 
|date=April 1970 |volume=34 |issue=1 |pages=136–172 |doi=10.1016/0022-2852(70)90080-9 |bibcode=1970JMoSp..34..136H}} This paper introduced a [[Hamiltonian (quantum mechanics)|Hamiltonian]] that has come to be called the Hougen-[[Philip Bunker|Bunker]]-Johns (HBJ) Hamiltonian.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/5.0016365|title="Derivation of 𝝆-dependent coordinate transformations for nonrigid molecules in the Hougen–Bunker–Johns formalism", J. Chem. Phys. 153, 084102 (2020)|journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=28 August 2020 |volume=153 |issue=8 |page=084102 |doi=10.1063/5.0016365 |language=en|last1=Viglaska |first1=Dominika |last2=Rey |first2=Michael |last3=Nikitin |first3=Andrei V. |last4=Tyuterev |first4=Vladimir G. |pmid=32872870 |s2cid=221466399 }}</ref>
*{{cite journal |last1=Hougen |first1=Jon T. |title=Classification of Rotational Energy Levels for Symmetric‐Top Molecules |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=October 1962 |volume=37 |issue=7 |pages=1433–1441 |doi=10.1063/1.1733301 |bibcode=1962JChPh..37.1433H }}

== Hobbies ==
He spoke several languages: French, French-Canadian, German, Czech, Japanese, and Mandarin in addition to English.<ref name=":0" />

== Awards and honors ==
Hougen was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 1979. In addition, Hougen received the following awards:

* [[Coblentz Award]] (1968)<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.coblentz.org/awards/the-coblentz-award|title=The Coblentz Award - The Coblentz Society|website=www.coblentz.org|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref>
* NBS Silver Medal (1974)<ref name=":0" />
* NBS Gold Medal (1980)<ref name=":0" />
* [[Ellis R. Lippincott Award]] (1984)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.osa.org/en-us/awards_and_grants/awards/award_description/ellislippincott/|title=Ellis R. Lippincott Award|last=|first=|date=|website=|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref>
* [[Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy]] (1984)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/plyler.cfm|title=Earle K. Plyler Prize for Molecular Spectroscopy & Dynamics|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref>
* Marcus Marci Award from the Czech Spectroscopy Society (1990)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vscht.cz/veda-a-vyzkum/ceny-a-souteze/ceny-udelene/medaile-emila-votocka/28548|title=Dr. Jon T. Hougen - Vysoká škola chemicko-technologická v Praze|website=www.vscht.cz|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref>

The ''[[Journal of Molecular Spectroscopy]]'' dedicated two special issues to him in honor of his 68th and 80th birthday.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-molecular-spectroscopy/vol/228/issue/2|title=Special Issue Dedicated to Dr. Jon T. Hougen on the Occasion of His 68th Birthday|website=www.sciencedirect.com|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-molecular-spectroscopy/vol/342/suppl/C|title=Spectroscopy of Large Amplitude Vibrational Motions, on the Occasion of Jon Hougen's 80th Birthday - Part I|website=www.sciencedirect.com|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/journal-of-molecular-spectroscopy/vol/343/suppl/C|title=Spectroscopy of Large Amplitude Vibrational Motion, on the Occasion of Jon Hougen's 80th Birthday – Part II|website=www.sciencedirect.com|access-date=2019-02-17}}</ref> 

Two awards were created in his memory: the Jon Hougen Travel Award for the 26th Colloquium on High-Resolution Molecular Spectroscopy (2019)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hrms2019.sciencesconf.org/resource/page/id/17|title=26th Colloquium on High-Resolution Molecular Spectroscopy - Sciencesconf.org|website=hrms2019.sciencesconf.org|access-date=2019-08-22}}</ref> and the Jon Hougen Memorial Award, awarded annually at the International Symposium on Molecular Spectroscopy (2020-present).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://isms.illinois.edu/HougenAward.php|title=International Symposium on Molecular Spectroscopy at Urbana-Champaign|website=isms.illinois.edu|access-date=2019-08-22}}</ref>
